purpose: Bounded numerical audit of completed run files; no models rerun and no paper files edited.

estimator.trial_mask: t>=2; each 80-trial episode contributes 79 trials per cover story
estimator.counterbalancing: For each base episode, trial, arm and cover story, average A-relative aligned logits across original and counterbalanced copy before scoring the higher-logit answer. Correct=1, incorrect=0, exact tie=.5.
estimator.pooling: Mean trial accuracy within each base episode and cover story; equal-weight mean of pet and assigned non-pet cover-story accuracy; mean across base episode pairs.

uncertainty.unit: base episode pair, jointly preserving both cover stories and both counterbalanced copies
uncertainty.bootstrap: Percentile CI for equally weighted mean: np.random.default_rng(seed).integers(0,n,size=(10000,n)); quantiles .025 and .975.
uncertainty.paired_contrast: summary minus raw per base pair, then bootstrap paired differences
uncertainty.wilcoxon: two-sided scipy.stats.wilcoxon(d,zero_method=wilcox), method default auto; unadjusted unless explicitly labelled Holm
uncertainty.holm_family: Only three completed larger-model compact p2 summary-minus-raw contrasts; exploratory, separate from original primary family.

sampled_image_fit_correction.definition: Read existing native sampled-choice fits: each model/game uses median over 20 sampled binary-choice sequence fits. Human comparisons use paired participant slopes and participant-bootstrap median difference, separate from episode-pair mean bootstrap above. Soft-target fields retained only to identify superseded manuscript numbers.

paired_sampled_model_vs_human_phi_slope.definition: Per-participant OLS slope of phi (xiong_mf) on h, model minus human, paired over the participants (same within-game choice and feedback histories). Model phi = median over S sampled binary choice sequences per episode; human phi = fit to the actual binary choices. Wilcoxon signed-rank on the paired differences + participant-bootstrap 95% CI of the median difference. Primary model condition: hazard_info = hidden. Humans were TOLD h and had prior task experience (1,600 / 3,200 trials before games 3 / 5), so the hidden-model vs told-human difference is a DESCRIPTIVE cross-condition difference, not by itself evidence of a human-model learning gap. Reported with it: model told vs human told (hazard information matched, experience still not) and the same-model told - hidden contrast.
paired_sampled_model_vs_human_phi_slope.comparison: descriptive cross-condition difference: model hazard-HIDDEN vs human hazard-TOLD (hazard information and prior experience both differ)

mc_error_of_draws.method: within-episode bootstrap of the S draws (n_rep=200)

design.truth: per-participant xiong_mf fits of the real humans per h (phi clipped to (0.01, 0.9), beta to (0.05, 4.0), |kappa|,|b| <= 3.0); simulated humans play closed loop on the real value sequences; model = same strategy with phi_h + delta*(h - mean h), replayed teacher-forced on the simulated human history; complete pipeline (pooled warm starts, 20-draw medians, Wilcoxon + bootstrap CI of the median paired slope difference). single_draw = the same test using only the first draw.

scope_and_limits: Compact p2 uses 16 development episode pairs; exploratory completed runs, not held-out replication.

These compact and CP-raw runs used H200; original 8B wording checks used RTX3090, and some original-layout development baselines were MI300X. Cross-layout contrasts must not silently imply matched hardware.
CP-raw uses all 48 held-out episode pairs and both cover stories. No new model-selection or mechanism claim follows.
No Thinking checkpoint result is introduced.
Psych101 JSON retains older soft-target summaries as well as sampled fits; sampled-choice manuscript claims must use sampled_fit and matching sampled contrast fields.
